channel.title: Blockchain Today
channel.description: Blockchain Today reports crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation and network upgrades, with analysis of what changed.

item.title: Fairshake commits $6 million across six House races
item.description: Fairshake is backing 32 House incumbents, six with $1 million each, as Senate gridlock over the CLARITY Act shifts crypto’s campaign push toward November races.

item.title: Zcash tests 25-second blocks ahead of planned November upgrade
item.description: Zcash activated NU7 on public testnet, cutting target blocks from 75 to 25 seconds and giving operators time to test before a possible November mainnet rollout.

item.title: Zcash activates 25-second blocks on public testnet early
item.description: Zcash activated NU7 on public testnet at block 4,465,026 on Oct. 4, testing 25-second blocks and new consensus rules before a mainnet decision.

item.title: Why an Ethereum-to-Polygon Deposit Can Still Be Pending
item.description: An Ethereum-to-Polygon deposit has two stages: Ethereum records the lock, then Polygon credits the matching asset; the status tells you which side to check.

item.title: A Bridge Rounding Error Is a Reason to Check Before Retrying
item.description: A displayed amount can hide a precision mismatch or an unfinished transfer; check the token units, transaction status and route before paying to try again.

item.title: A TRON QR request has two clocks: wallet approval and confirmation
item.description: A QR scan only starts the wallet exchange. Approval, broadcast and TRON confirmation each take a different amount of time, for different reasons.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional crypto self-custody for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC has proposed conditional self-custody and state trust companies for adviser and fund crypto holdings, widening custody options while setting new safeguards.

item.title: How to Turn Airdrop Proceeds Into Home-Chain Stablecoins
item.description: Airdrop proceeds become home-chain stablecoins through a claim, a local sale, and a cross-chain transfer; fees, token form, and destination liquidity decide the route.

item.title: A pending TRON USDT transfer needs a status check first
item.description: A TRON USDT transfer can look pending after broadcast without being confirmed; check its transaction ID, final receipt and expiration before deciding whether to retry.

item.title: A Pending Avalanche Swap Needs a Nonce Check Before Replacement
item.description: A pending Avalanche swap is not a failed trade. Check its nonce, fee fields and status before deciding whether to speed it up, cancel it or wait.

item.title: Why Polygon Bridge Claims Match the Burned Amount
item.description: Polygon PoS withdrawals use a verified burn event to determine how much escrowed token can be claimed on Ethereum, with checkpoints adding time and proof steps.

item.title: Funding one liquidity pool from two chains
item.description: A cross-chain pool needs shared accounting and settlement rules. Learn how deposits reach one position, what ordinary AMMs cannot do, and what to check first.

item.title: Why Source-Chain Refunds Take Time
item.description: A source-chain refund can wait on swap retries, signing and the source network’s confirmation rules; the status trail shows which stage is still pending.

item.title: A Destination Confirmation Is One Step in a Cross-Chain Transfer
item.description: A destination-chain confirmation shows that the receiving network recorded an action, but it does not alone prove the source transfer is final or the bridge flow is complete.

item.title: How to Choose a Network for Stablecoins
item.description: Choose a stablecoin network by checking the exact token, destination support, total transfer cost and settlement needs; low fees matter only if the asset arrives usable.

item.title: Three Checks Before Claiming a Polygon PoS Withdrawal
item.description: A Polygon PoS withdrawal is a burn, checkpoint and Ethereum exit: verify the route, match the burn record, then confirm the final claim and Ethereum fee.

item.title: The Destination Network Is Part of the Swap
item.description: A destination network is part of the address, not a detail to infer from a token ticker; verify chain, asset form and recipient before you approve.

item.title: Budgeting Energy for a TRON Swap Starts With a Live Estimate
item.description: Budget a TRON swap from a live Energy estimate, your available resources and a capped TRX fallback; pool activity and contract settings can change the final bill for each trade.

item.title: A holder count needs a dust line
item.description: A holder count treats every nonzero wallet alike; a dust-adjusted count sets a balance cutoff, making token growth easier to compare while exposing the threshold.

item.title: Getting Stablecoins onto Polygon Before Checkout
item.description: The route depends on where your stablecoin sits: use a supported Polygon withdrawal when available, or bridge it, then verify the checkout network, token and fee balance.
